doc: docs/RPG_SPEC.json — items, equipment, inventory, weapon families and weapon physics for EMBERGATE (repo slug stays 'gatebreaker'). Design only. NOTHING in src/ was changed to produce this document; every claim about the code below was read out of the tree at commit 'Camera: un-invert the tilt, widen it, and pull back' (versionCode 7 / 1.6-camera).
ownerBrief: Verbatim: 'I want the characters to properly hold the swords and when they are in the plaza, the sword can be visible or placed in the inventory. allow an inventory button that display everything about the character, and where they can change the weapons and armor slots. each having different benefits and if they collect a set it will make the overall armor pieces more powerful. if we have different weapons, like bow and arrows, daggers, swords, great sword, axes and so on... the legendary ones should be harder to develop but more powerful... make sure the weapons follow the right physics in a magic world.'
summary: Seven asks, one system. The spine of it is a finding, not a feature: src/game/weapons.js already contains a complete, per-archetype swing state machine — windup / active / recovery / lock / cancel / lunge / stagger / move-scale, hand-tuned per family — and NOTHING OUTSIDE THAT FILE IMPORTS ANY OF IT (verified by grep across src/ and tools/: zero external consumers of makeAttackState, startAttack, tickAttack, canAttack, consumeLunge, moveScale, isCommitted, attackPhase, attackAnim, hitDamage, hitRange, hitArc, hitKnockback, hitStagger, isRadial, weaponSummary or ARCHETYPES). game.js._applySwingDamage still runs the original hardcoded three-chop sword (p.comboIndex, p.swing = 0.34, ranges 2.9/3.6, arcs 0.62pi/0.85pi, knock 2.5/9) and merely multiplies the equipped weapon's dmgMul / reachMul / arcMul / knockMul on top. The consequence is exactly the thing the owner noticed: EVERY WEAPON CURRENTLY SWINGS LIKE A SWORD. A greataxe does bigger numbers on identical timing. So 'make sure the weapons follow the right physics' is roughly ninety percent a WIRING job against code that already exists and was already tuned, and only ten percent new content. That wiring is STEP 1 and it ships alone. On top of it this spec defines: an 8-slot equipment model (weapon, offhand, head, chest, hands, legs, feet, trinket) persisted with the same four-field (base, rarity, seed, level) trick weapons already use, so armor costs the save file almost nothing and re-tuning the tables re-derives everyone's gear; five armor sets with 2 / 4 / 5-piece thresholds where the partials are small flat numbers and the full-set bonus is a RULE rather than a multiplier (that asymmetry is the whole anti-power-creep argument, and it is backed by a hard 0.72 total damage-reduction clamp); seven weapon families mapped ONLY onto models that actually exist in the shipped packs (and an explicit, uncomfortable admission that items.glb contains no staff, no wand, no spear, no shield, no helmet and no boots); a mass-and-momentum law for weapon feel that magic is allowed to bend in exactly two named ways and no others; a legendary tier that is gated by WHERE you have been rather than by luck, and completed by an Ascension craft; a two-column inventory panel designed against the 412 px-tall landscape phone viewport that already forced the Exchange into a scroll box; and a stow/draw stance that re-parents the existing weapon group between a hand socket and a new chest socket without creating or disposing a single geometry — because weapons.js's own header documents that dropping a material costs an 8-60 ms shader recompile on a mid-range Android. Wave 3-A WAS steps 2-6 — step 1 was planned for it, was not built, and has moved to 3-B. Wave 3-B is step 1 first, then steps 7-14. See waveSplit and buildOrder[0].status; step 7 records the dependency.

swingStateMachineIsDark: src/game/weapons.js exports a full attack state machine — makeAttackState, currentStep, canAttack, startAttack, tickAttack, consumeBuffer, consumeLunge, cancelAttack, moveScale, isCommitted, attackPhase, attackAnim — plus the hit-maths helpers hitDamage/hitRange/hitArc/hitKnockback/hitStagger/isRadial and the presentation helper weaponSummary. `grep -rn` over src/ and tools/, excluding weapons.js itself, returns ZERO matches for all of them.

src/game/game.js:930-963 (_startSwing / _applySwingDamage) is still the pre-weapons.js implementation: p.comboIndex cycling 1..3, p.swing = 0.34, p.comboTimer = 0.95, finisher x1.85, range (finisher ? 3.6 : 2.9), arc (finisher ? PI*0.85 : PI*0.62), knockback (finisher ? 9 : 2.5), stagger finisher-only 0.45. The equipped weapon contributes ONLY w.dmgMul, w.reachMul, w.arcMul, w.knockMul.

Therefore: the GREATAXE_COMBO / MAUL_COMBO / DAGGER_COMBO / SPEAR_COMBO / GLAIVE_COMBO tables, the per-archetype lock and cancel windows, the per-step move multipliers, the lunge impulses, the multi-hit dagger finisher and the radial maul pound are all authored, tested-by-eye at authoring time, and UNREACHABLE. This is the single highest-value change in the whole document and it is a deletion-plus-rewiring, not new content.

The comment at weapons.js:218 states the intent plainly: 'The current hardcoded sword — windup 0.17, total 0.34, ranges 2.9/3.6, arcs 0.62pi/0.85pi, knockback 2.5/9, finisher x1.85 — is exactly `riftedge` below, so switching game.js over to this table is a no-op for existing feel.' That sentence is the acceptance criterion for STEP 1, and it should be asserted numerically rather than trusted.
shippedItemModels: public/models/items.json DOES NOT EXIST. The brief named it; the tree has public/models/items.glb (736 KB) plus public/models/icons.json (108 icon keys) + icons.webp. The authoritative model inventory is the source pack folder 'Ultimate RPG Items Pack - Aug 2019/OBJ/' (106 .obj files, gitignored source per ASSETS.md:171) and the runtime index built by src/render/models.js (listItems()). All 106 names below were read off that folder, not guessed.

WEAPON-CAPABLE MODELS THAT ACTUALLY EXIST: Sword, Sword_Golden, Sword_big, Sword_big_Golden, Axe_small, Axe_small_Golden, Axe_Double, Axe_Double_Golden, Hammer_Double, Hammer_Double_Golden, Dagger, Dagger_Golden, Bow_Wooden, Bow_Golden, Arrow, Arrow_Golden, Dart, Dart_Golden.

OTHER 106-pack contents, listed so nobody re-derives them: Backpack, Bag, Bone, Book1..4 (Closed/Open), Chalice, Chest_Closed/Open/Ingots, ChickenLeg, Coin, Coin_Skull, Coin_Star, Crystal1..Crystal5 (+ _Damaged variants for 1,2,3,5), FishBone, Gold_Ingots, Heart, Heart_Broken, Heart_Half, Key1..4, Mineral, Padlock, Parchment, Potion1..Potion11 (Empty/Filled), Pouch, Scroll, Skull, Skull2, Snowflake1..3, Star.

public/models/adventurers.glb (789 KB, KayKit Adventurers, CC0) DOES contain adv_staff, adv_bow, adv_quiver, adv_arrow, adv_shield_badge, adv_sword_1h, adv_axe_2h, adv_dagger. BUT adventurers.json's own note reads 'Deliverable only this wave: no src/ consumer exists yet', every prop is namespaced under a specific character's handslot node (adv_staff lives under mage_handslot_r), and every clip is namespaced per character because GLTFLoader renames duplicate node names on load. Harvesting a staff from it is a new loader path, not a lookup. Recommended: do not put it on the critical path (see weaponFamilies.staff).
iconAtlasIsAlreadyTheInventoryUI: src/ui/icons.js is finished and unused by any panel: loadIconIndex(), hasIcon(), iconStyle(name, size), iconEl(name, size). 108 lowercase keys in a single 1408x1280 WebP (~310 KB), one image and one request for the whole inventory.

iconStyle() already returns a neutral grey square for an unknown name — so an EMPTY SLOT and a MISSING ICON render identically and correctly with zero extra code. Build the slot grid on top of that behaviour rather than writing placeholder markup.

Icon keys that matter here: sword, sword_golden, sword_big, sword_big_golden, axe_small, axe_small_golden, axe_double, axe_double_golden, hammer_double, hammer_double_golden, dagger, dagger_golden, bow_wooden, bow_golden, arrow, arrow_golden, armor_leather, armor_metal, armor_metal2, armor_black, armor_golden, glove, crown, crown2, necklace1..3, ring1..7, crystal1..5, mineral, chalice, scroll, book1_closed. Every one verified present in icons.json.
characterRigAndSockets: src/render/characters.js:1037-1047 builds exactly THREE sockets: sockets.hand (m_Wrist_R / f_Wrist_R, lift 0.72, scale 1/MODEL_SCALE), sockets.handL (Wrist_L, same), sockets.head (Head, lift 0, scale 1). There is NO back socket and NO hip socket, so nothing can currently be stowed.

The 62-bone list in public/models/characters.json DOES contain m_Chest, m_Torso, m_Abdomen and m_Hips (and the f_ equivalents). makeSocket(bone, {lift, scale}) is generic and re-usable — a back socket is `makeSocket(getObjectByName(p + 'Chest'), { lift: 0, scale: 1 / MODEL_SCALE })` and a hip socket is the same off 'Hips'. No new asset, no new maths.

The procedural box-man (entities.js makeHumanoid) has rig.body / rig.torso / rig.armL / rig.armR / rig.legL / rig.legR. Its stow fallback is rig.torso for the back and rig.body for the hips. Both paths must work: the game is required to boot with public/models/ deleted.

CharacterInstance.setArmed(armed) already swaps the idle clip between Idle_Sword and the neutral arms-down idle, and invalidates the cached 'idle' action so the change takes effect immediately. Sheathing therefore gets the correct relaxed plaza walk FOR FREE — it is one setArmed(false) call.

There is exactly ONE armed idle clip in the pack (`*_Idle_Sword`). There is no armed-with-bow and no armed-with-staff idle. A bow user will stand in a sword idle. At play distance on a phone this is acceptable; a small additive left-arm offset is the cheap fix if it reads wrong, and a new clip is not on the table.
armorHasNoWearableGeometry: Consequence of shippedItemModels: there is no helmet mesh, no boot mesh, no greave mesh and no wearable cuirass. items.glb's Armor_* are prop-scale standalone models (display armour), not rig-fitted garments. They cannot be parented to a bone and look like clothing.

The only honest 3D expression of armour in this tree is the MODULAR CHARACTER PART SWAP that characters.js already implements: public/models/characters.json declares slots ['head','body','legs','feet','backpack','pistol'] across 21 characters over 2 shared rigs, and characters.js:40 states 'PARTS ARE SWAPPABLE WITHIN A PACK. head/body/legs/feet from any character' — appearanceFor() already mixes them per-seed to stop enemies being one body in six colours.

COST WARNING, and it is a real one: characters.js merges the four chosen parts into ONE geometry keyed by `${rig}|${head}|${body}|${legs}|${feet}` and refcounts it via releaseGeometry(). Every DISTINCT armour look is one more merged geometry resident in the cache. Twenty-five set looks across a crowd would be twenty-five merges. Armour visuals must therefore be PLAYER-ONLY. Enemies and shadow soldiers keep their seeded appearance and gain nothing from armour.
saveAndLoadoutSeams: src/core/save.js: SCHEMA_VERSION 2, key 'gatebreaker.save.v2', legacy 'gatebreaker.save.v1' deliberately left in place after upgrade so a rollback finds a profile. migrate() is pure and total.

The file states the bump rule explicitly, twice (save.shop and save.worldTime): 'Deliberately NOT a schema bump: an absent value is indistinguishable from this one.' A CHANGED FIELD TYPE is what forced v1 -> v2. save.equipment is a NEW field with an absent-reads-as-default meaning, so it follows the shop precedent — ensureEquipment(save) is the migration, idempotent, called first by every entry point, exactly like ensureShopSave(save).
Today: save.weapon is a single {b,r,s,l} record and save.stash is an array of the same. game.js:322-361 owns both — _restoreLoadout / _persistLoadout / equip. STASH_LIMIT is 12 (game.js:48).

BUG THAT BECOMES SERIOUS WITH EIGHT SLOTS: game.equip(w) unconditionally unshifts the outgoing weapon onto the stash. Equipping an item that CAME FROM the stash therefore leaves a duplicate — the stash entry is never removed. With one slot and a 12-entry cap this self-heals by eviction. With eight slots and a 40-entry cap it is a duplication exploit. equipSlot() must SWAP: remove the incoming instance from the stash, push the outgoing one.
STASH_LIMIT 12 is far too small once armour drops. One D-rank dungeon can produce five armour pieces. Raise to 40; the storage cost is 40 x 4 short fields.
projectileSystemIsNotReadyForBows: game.js:1139 _spawnProjectile allocates PER SHOT: `new THREE.IcosahedronGeometry(0.3, 0)`, `new THREE.MeshBasicMaterial({color})`, and `new THREE.PointLight(color, 2.2, 7)` parented to the bolt. _removeProjectile disposes the geometry and material. At caster pace (attackCd 2.6) this is invisible. At bow pace (three shots a second, a dozen in flight) it is a per-shot material creation — which by weapons.js's own measured note costs a shader program lookup and, on a cold path, 8-60 ms — plus up to a dozen simultaneous dynamic point lights, which is a phone-GPU cliff, not a cost.

game.js:1667 _updateProjectiles integrates FLAT: `dir` is built with `.setY(0).normalize()` at spawn and the position is `pos.addScaledVector(dir, speed * dt)`. There is no vertical velocity and no gravity. Arrow flight is a genuine addition to this loop, not a parameter change.

Collision already does the right thing and must not be rewritten: the bolt dies on `this.world.obstacleField?.blocked(pr.pos.x, pr.pos.z, 0.25, 0, pr.pos.y)` — the projectile's own height is the feetY, so kerb-height crates (top 0.4) do not eat shots while walls (top Infinity) always block. The `hypot(x,z) > world.radius + 2` disc cull is the outer bound in both worlds.

src/world/obstacles.js:562 lineBlocked(x0,z0,x1,z1,{step=1.2,radius=0.2,feetY=1.2}) is the SEGMENT probe, and its header is explicit that it is for throttled use ('callers throttle (the AI probes on a 0.4 s cadence), never per-frame across the whole field'). Its internal sample spacing is clamped to 2*radius + 0.5 so a 0.6 m dungeon wall cannot leak a shot between samples. Use it ONCE at release for target validation / soft-lock, never per frame per arrow.
gpuAndDrawCallDiscipline: weapons.js mergedItemGeometry(name) is the pattern that must be reused for anything new that gets held or fired: every items.glb weapon is 4-5 primitives split by flat colour, and handing one straight to an NPC cost 4-5 draw calls where the old procedural plank cost 1 — tools/character-test.mjs caught a 21-strong crowd going from 5 to 8.05 calls per character. The fix bakes each primitive's flat colour into a Uint8 vertex-colour attribute and merges to ONE geometry against ONE shared material, cached by item name for the life of the process.

That path has two non-obvious hard-won details that any new item must inherit: toFloatAttribute() must float the quantised POSITION/NORMAL before applyMatrix4 (items.glb is KHR_mesh_quantization; writing float results back into a Uint16 array truncated every vertex to almost-zero and rendered armed enemies EMPTY-HANDED in a shipped build), and heldMaterial() must be THREE.DoubleSide because several items.glb nodes carry mirrored (negative-determinant) transforms whose winding flips on bake — under FrontSide those weapons back-face-culled to nothing.

weapons.js's geometry and material caches are flagged `userData.shared = true` and are NEVER disposed mid-run, because entity teardown frees anything unflagged it can reach. Any new cache (armour part geometry, arrow geometry, stow transforms) must set the same flag or it will be freed out from under every other holder.

DUNGEON_SPEC budget is <= 24 draw calls and <= 130k tris. A stowed weapon plus a drawn weapon must be the SAME object re-parented, not two meshes with one hidden — a hidden mesh still costs a matrix update and a frustum test, and two meshes is how a stow feature turns into a permanent +1 draw call.
equipWeapon() deliberately never disposes on swap. Stow/draw must obey the same law: RE-PARENT ONLY.
uiLanguageAndViewport: src/ui/shopui.js is the closest sibling and the pattern to copy exactly: an OVERLAY toggled by classList, NOT an AppState screen — because AppState.go('city') calls Game.enterCity -> _setMode, which DISPOSES AND REBUILDS the whole city and teleports the player back to spawn. Closing an inventory panel must never do that.

It builds its own DOM and injects its own <style> so it shares neither a file nor a merge conflict with ui.js or styles.css, and it re-uses the SHIPPED classes rather than reinventing a look: .panel / .panel.wide / .panel-sub / .btn / .btn.ghost / .gate / .gate-list / .gate .meta / .gate .rank / .readout / .readout .row / .rank-E..rank-S. Colour tokens: --ink #e8ecff, --dim #8a93b8, --accent #7c5cff, --accent2 #22d3ee, --danger #ff4d6d, --gold #ffc24b, --edge rgba(124,92,255,.35).

Every node is built with createElement/textContent — the repo's standing rule is 'a markup sink is a markup sink whatever you believe about its inputs today'. Item names are generated by rollWeapon's buildName; that does not buy an innerHTML exemption.

THE VIEWPORT LESSON IS ALREADY PAID FOR. shopui.js's CSS carries this comment: 'Tighter than a gate row on purpose: a gate list is six entries and the shelf is eight, on a 412 px-tall landscape phone, inside a scroll box. The gate row's 44 px swatch and 13 px padding fit two rows in the window; this fits nearly four.' It shrank .gate padding to 9px 12px, the tier pill to 36px, and added `.shop-list { max-height: min(52vh, 360px); overflow-y: auto; }`. The inventory has strictly more content than the shop, so it needs a two-column landscape layout with independent scroll, not a longer single list.

z-index: #shop is 60 and adds body.gb-shop which hides #cityUi, because .screen is 20 and #cityUi is 40 and the live OPEN button would otherwise render on top of the panel and eat taps. The inventory must do the same.

src/main.js:126-136 handleBack() is the Android hardware-back chain; it checks `game.shopUI?.isOpen` and closes it before falling through to app.back(). The inventory needs one more line there, in front of the shop check if it can be opened over the shop (recommendation: it cannot — only one overlay at a time).
determinismContract: src/core/rng.js mulberry32 carries a do-not-touch warning: context-loss recovery rebuilds a gate via world.build(gate, seed), so the same seed MUST replay the exact same stream, and any change silently invalidates every saved seed plus the byte-compare soak in tools/dungeon-gen-test.mjs.

rollWeapon() is already seed-addressable: it consumes the stream in a FIXED order, and rollRarity is drawn even when a rarity was forced, precisely so a stored (base, rarity, seed, level) rebuilds byte-identically. rollArmor MUST be written as its exact structural twin or armour will drift on the first balance patch.

shop.js seeds its shelf from the rank band alone with a fixed salt (SHOP_SALT 0x5ade0f, band mixed with 0x9e3779b1) and consumes the stream for EVERY row including locked ones, so unlocking a row cannot re-roll the rows above it. Any new vendor or craft surface must pick its own salt and document it here.

equipmentSlots.recommendation: EIGHT slots: weapon, offhand, head, chest, hands, legs, feet, trinket. Five of them (head/chest/hands/legs/feet) are the ARMOR slots and are the only ones a set counts — which is what makes 2/4/5 clean thresholds. offhand and trinket are deliberately outside the set maths so there is always a free choice that no set can claim.
equipmentSlots.whyNotSix: Six slots (drop hands and trinket) gives 2/4/4 thresholds, which collapses the 4-piece and full-set tiers into the same decision. Ten slots (adding shoulders, belt, two rings) is more slots than the shipped icon set can distinguish at 40 px on a phone. Five armor slots is the smallest number that supports a real partial-set curve.

slots.name: WEAPON
slots.contributes: Everything about how combat FEELS: the family, hence the combo table, windup, recovery, lock, reach, arc, knockback, stagger, movement penalty, draw time. Plus dmgMul, rate, critAdd, critMul, leech from the roll.
slots.notes: Already exists as save.weapon. Its instance shape is unchanged. Twin daggers (archetype 'daggers') intrinsically consume the offhand — buildDaggers puts the second blade on group.userData.offhand and equipWeapon reparents it to handL. The offhand slot therefore LOCKS while a twin-dagger family is equipped, and the panel must say so rather than silently dropping the offhand item.

slots.name: OFFHAND
slots.contributes: Defensive or ammunition. Quiver (required by bow: +max nocked arrows, +draw speed), focus (staff: +mana, +bolt turn rate), or a parry token. NOT a shield in Wave 3-B — see openQuestions; there is no shield mesh in items.glb and adv_shield_badge is locked inside adventurers.glb behind a loader that does not exist.
slots.notes: Represent the quiver with the `arrow` / `arrow_golden` icon and the focus with `crystal2` / `mineral`. No 3D mesh in Wave 3-B: an offhand item is stats + icon only. The bow can be drawn with no quiver — the quiver is an upgrade, not a requirement, because a slot that can hard-disable your weapon is a trap.

slots.name: HEAD
slots.contributes: PERCEPTION-flavoured: +tellLeadMs (the enemy wind-up warning derive() already computes) and +critDmg. The 'I see it coming' slot.
slots.notes: Icons: crown, crown2, and for set-specific looks the pack has no helmets, so the head piece is expressed visually through the character part-swap head part, not through a worn mesh.

slots.name: CHEST
slots.contributes: The slab. Largest single armorDR contribution (SLOT_WEIGHT 1.00) and +maxHp. This is the slot a player upgrades first and feels immediately.
slots.notes: Icons: armor_leather, armor_metal, armor_metal2, armor_black, armor_golden — one per set, which is a lucky exact fit for the five sets below.

slots.name: HANDS
slots.contributes: Weapon handling: +atkSpeed (folded into the EXISTING STAT_RATES.str.atkSpeedCap of 0.30, never past it) and a small recovery shave on the current combo step.
slots.notes: The pack has exactly one glove model and one glove icon. All five sets share the `glove` icon tinted by rarity colour; that is honest and reads fine at 40 px.

slots.name: LEGS
slots.contributes: Mobility: +move speed and +dodgeWindow (the perfect-dodge window derive() computes from agility).
slots.notes: No leg model or leg icon exists. Reuse the set's chest icon at a lower saturation, or the `bag`/`pouch` icons as a legible stand-in. Flagged in openQuestions — this is the weakest icon mapping in the document and the owner should see it before it ships.

slots.name: FEET
slots.contributes: Footing: +staggerResist and −knockback taken. The slot that makes a heavy-weapon build survivable, because heavy weapons root you.
slots.notes: No boot model or boot icon. Same stand-in problem as legs. staggerResist is a NEW derived value (0..0.6) that game.js's stagger application must read; there is no existing field for it.

slots.name: TRINKET
slots.contributes: One exotic effect, no armorDR at all. Leech, ash-find, luck (feeds rollDrop's existing `luck` parameter), mana regen, or extraction chance (feeds progression.extractionChance's PER term).
slots.notes: The single best-supported slot in the pack: Ring1..Ring7 and Necklace1..Necklace3 = ten distinct models and ten distinct icons. Explicitly OUTSIDE the set maths, so there is always one slot a set cannot dictate.

dataModel.principle: An item DEFINITION is static, shared and read-only. An item INSTANCE is four short fields. Nothing else is ever persisted. This is not a new idea — it is the rule weapons.js already enforces ('Weapons are fully described by (base, rarity, seed, level) because rollWeapon consumes the stream in a fixed order — so the save file stores four fields instead of a snapshot that would drift the next time the tables are tuned') and armour must obey it identically or the two halves of the inventory will age differently.

definition.shape: { id, slot, family|setId, tier, minRank, reqLevel, icon, model|null, look, base<stat block>, blurb }
definition.livesIn: WEAPONS in src/game/weapons.js (unchanged) and a new ARMOR_BASES in src/game/armor.js
definition.ids: lowercase, no spaces, stable forever — an id in a save is a contract. Weapons already follow this (riftedge, dawnbrand, sunderaxe, gravemaul, whisperfangs, veinsplitters, vigil, voidglaive). Armour ids are `${setId}_${slot}`: issue_chest, ossuary_feet, vigil_head, and so on.

fields.k: kind. 'w' weapon, 'a' armor, 't' trinket. ABSENT MEANS 'w' — that absence IS the migration for every stash entry ever written.
fields.l: level the item was rolled at

instance.note: Byte-compatible with today's serializeWeapon output, which emits {b,r,s,l} and no k. deserializeItem reads k ?? 'w'.

savePersistence.newField: save.equipment = { weapon: null, offhand: null, head: null, chest: null, hands: null, legs: null, feet: null, trinket: null } — each null or an instance record.
savePersistence.schemaBump: NONE. Follow the save.shop / save.worldTime precedent verbatim: an absent value is indistinguishable from the default, so ensureEquipment(save) is the migration and it runs on first contact from every entry point. SCHEMA_VERSION stays 2.
migrationPath: ensureEquipment(save): if save.equipment is missing or not an object, create the eight-key object with all nulls.
If save.equipment.weapon is null AND save.weapon is a valid record, COPY save.weapon into save.equipment.weapon. That is the entire v-old -> v-new upgrade for the one slot that already existed.

Sanitise structurally only (does b look like a string, is s a finite number) and NEVER import weapons.js from save.js — save.js deliberately does not pull THREE in to validate a string, and sanitiseShop() is the precedent.
Filter save.stash: entries lacking k get k:'w'; entries whose k is unknown are dropped, not thrown on.
savePersistence.dualWrite: _persistLoadout MUST keep writing save.weapon as a mirror of save.equipment.weapon. A build rolled back to the shipped version reads save.weapon and finds the right sword. Dropping the mirror is how a rollback loses a player's weapon, and save.js's own comment about leaving the v1 key in place is the precedent for caring about this.
savePersistence.stashLimit: 12 -> 40. Armour fills 12 in a single D-rank dungeon. 40 records x 5 short fields is nothing in localStorage.

invariants: An instance never appears in two places at once. equipSlot(save, slot, instance) removes it from the stash and pushes the outgoing one — SWAP, never push-only. This closes the duplication hole described in auditFindings.saveAndLoadoutSeams.

Equipping is refused, with a reason string in the shop's language ('REQUIRES LEVEL 14', 'B-GRADE HUNTERS ONLY'), when base.reqLevel > save.level or base.minRank > shopBand(save). Reuse shop.js's shopBand and its exact wording so two panels do not disagree about the same rule.
Every derived number is recomputed from (save, equipment) on equip. Nothing caches a stat line, because a stat line is exactly the thing that drifts when tables are tuned.
armor.js and equipment.js are THREE-free and DOM-free, like config.js / progression.js / shop.js, so they can be driven headless by node.

armorSets.identification: Each armour base carries setId. A set is counted over the FIVE armour slots only (head, chest, hands, legs, feet). Offhand and trinket never count. setProgress(equipment) returns a Map of setId -> count, which is all the UI and the bonus resolver need.

armorPoints.rarityMultiplier: Reuse the SHIPPED RARITIES table (common 1.00, uncommon 1.09, rare 1.20, epic 1.36, legendary 1.58). Do not invent a second rarity ladder; two ladders is how a weapon rare and an armour rare stop meaning the same thing.

damageReduction.why: A soft curve that asymptotes below 1 and whose denominator grows with level, so a tier-1 set decays into irrelevance without any explicit expiry rule. No clamp is needed on the term itself; the clamp lives on the TOTAL.
workedExamples: Full tier-1 common set at L5: AP = 12 * 3.30 = 39.6; denominator 39.6 + 90 + 130 = 259.6; armorDR = 15.3%.
Full tier-3 common set at L20: AP = 36 * 3.30 = 118.8; denominator 118.8 + 90 + 520 = 728.8; armorDR = 16.3%.
Full tier-3 EPIC set at L20: AP = 118.8 * 1.36 = 161.6; denominator 161.6 + 610 = 771.6; armorDR = 20.9%.
Full tier-5 legendary set at L60: AP = 80 * 3.30 * 1.58 = 417.1; denominator 417.1 + 90 + 1560 = 2067.1; armorDR = 20.2%.
Read the shape: armorDR sits in a 15-21% band across the WHOLE game. Armour is a steady, legible, never-runaway layer. The excitement comes from the set RULES and the affixes, not from the slab.
damageReduction.stacking: MULTIPLICATIVE with the existing vitality DR: taken = raw * (1 - derive().dr) * (1 - armorDR). Then a HARD CLAMP: total reduction may never exceed 0.72, i.e. taken >= raw * 0.28. derive().dr already caps at 0.45; 0.45 and 0.21 multiply to 0.565, so the clamp is headroom for affixes and set rules rather than a wall the honest builds hit.

secondaryBySlot.head: tellLeadMs +6 * tier (on top of derive().tellLeadMs, still clamped by STAT_RATES.per.tellCapMs 520); critDmg +0.02 * tier
secondaryBySlot.chest: maxHp +9 * tier; carries the largest SLOT_WEIGHT so it is also the DR slot
secondaryBySlot.hands: atkSpeed +0.012 * tier, folded into the EXISTING STAT_RATES.str.atkSpeedCap of 0.30
secondaryBySlot.legs: speed +0.045 * tier, with a HARD armour-speed cap of +0.6 u/s across all sources; dodgeWindow +0.008 * tier s, clamped by the existing dodgeCapMs 260
secondaryBySlot.feet: staggerResist +0.06 * tier (NEW derived value, clamp 0.60); knockback taken -0.05 * tier (clamp 0.50)
secondaryBySlot.trinket: no AP, no secondary — one rolled exotic affix only

affixes.count: Reuse RARITIES[r].affixes exactly: common 0, uncommon 1, rare 2, epic 3, legendary 4.
affixes.pool: A SEPARATE ARMOR_AFFIXES table, because the shipped AFFIXES all mutate weapon fields (dmgMul, rate, critAdd, knockMul, reachMul, leech) and would be meaningless on a boot.
affixes.note: Same lo/hi/apply(target, magnitude) contract the weapon affixes use, drawn without replacement from a pool copy, so rollArmor is a structural clone of rollWeapon and the two stay in step forever.

armorSets.setBonusLaw: PARTIAL BONUSES ARE SMALL FLAT NUMBERS. THE FULL-SET BONUS IS A RULE, NOT A NUMBER. This asymmetry is the entire anti-trivialisation argument and it should be stated in the armor.js header. A number can be stacked, multiplied, and compared against a bigger number; a rule cannot be stacked with itself, and you only have five armour slots so exactly one full-set rule can ever be live. Meanwhile two 2-piece partials (from two different sets) are deliberately allowed and deliberately competitive — 6% + 6% is a real choice against one 5-piece rule, and that tension is the interesting part of the system. Set bonuses do NOT scale with rarity or with level. A legendary set piece is better than a common one through AP and affixes only.

This is the one genuinely new animation work in the whole spec.

weaponPhysics.law: MASS IS REAL. ENCHANTMENT IS NOT MASS. Every weapon has a mass and a moment of inertia. Mass sets windup, recovery, lock, movement penalty, stagger, knockback and draw time — and NOTHING in the game may push any of those below the family's floor. Enchantment changes what the damage IS (fire, void, bleed, void-rend), adds effects (leech, chain, hook, detonation), and may bend a TRAJECTORY (a bolt that steers, a blade that curves) — but it never makes a greataxe light. A legendary greataxe hits harder, burns, and cracks the floor. It still swings like a greataxe. This is the rule because weight is the only thing the player's hands can learn; if magic were allowed to void it, the hands would stop learning and every weapon would collapse back into the same weapon with different numbers — which, as auditFindings records, is EXACTLY the state the game is in today.
magicMayBendExactlyTwoThings: 1. DAMAGE TYPE AND EFFECT. An enchantment may change what a hit does after it lands. It may never change how long the hit took to arrive or how long you are stuck afterwards.

2. TRAJECTORY CURVATURE, BOUNDED. A magic projectile may steer, up to a stated maximum turn rate (90 deg/s for the staff bolt, 0 for arrows). It may not teleport, it may not ignore gravity, and it may not exceed its family's launch speed. A fast-moving target can therefore still outrun a homing bolt, which is what keeps 'homing' a property rather than a guarantee.

authoringFormulaForNewFamiliesOnly.lock: windup + active + recovery for mass >= 4.0 (full commitment); windup + 0.55 * recovery below that
authoringFormulaForNewFamiliesOnly.stagger: 0.09 * mass on an opener, 0.19 * mass on a finisher
authoringFormulaForNewFamiliesOnly.knockback: 2.1 * mass on an opener, 4.0 * mass on a finisher
authoringFormulaForNewFamiliesOnly.hitStop: 0.019 * mass on a connecting finisher, 0 on openers below mass 2.0

The SHIPPED tables (SWORD_COMBO, GREATAXE_COMBO, MAUL_COMBO, DAGGER_COMBO, SPEAR_COMBO, GLAIVE_COMBO) must be left byte-identical. They were hand-tuned, and regenerating them from a formula would drift the one thing the owner has already approved. If a formula disagrees with a shipped number, the formula is wrong.

whatThePlayerActuallyFEELS.commitment: isCommitted(state, w) already returns true while state.t < step.lock, and the intent is that dash and every other escape is REFUSED while it holds. Wiring that is what makes a greataxe swing frightening: you press, and for 0.90 s you are a statue with an axe in the air. A dagger's lock equals its windup (0.075 s), so you are effectively never trapped. This one boolean is the largest single contributor to 'weight' in the entire game and it currently does nothing because nothing calls it.
whatThePlayerActuallyFEELS.recoveryIsThePunishment: Recovery is tuned against enemy attack cooldowns, and the relationship is deliberate: grunt attackCd is 1.5 s and stalker is 1.2 s (config.ENEMY_TYPES). A whiffed greataxe finisher costs 0.55 windup + 0.16 active + 0.52 recovery = 1.23 s, which is almost exactly one free enemy attack. A whiffed dagger light costs 0.18 s, which is nothing. State this relationship in the code so a future tuner does not break it by accident.
whatThePlayerActuallyFEELS.momentumCarry: Today `state.lunge = step.lunge` is set once at step start and consumed as a single impulse (startAttack + consumeLunge). Heavy weapons should CARRY: the impulse spread across windup into active, so the body visibly leans into the swing and arrives with the blade instead of teleporting first. Add `lungeCurve: 'impulse' | 'carry'` to the step; 'carry' distributes lunge over (windup + active) with an ease-in. Cheap — one field, one lerp in consumeLunge — and it is the difference between a big swing and a big swing that has weight behind it.
whatThePlayerActuallyFEELS.reachIsGeometryNotAStat: A family's `range` must be within 0.5 m of its model's ACTUAL tip distance: itemBounds(name).y * MODEL_SCALE[family] + 0.72 * rigScale. models.js exports itemBounds() specifically for 'reach/socket tuning' and nothing uses it. Make it an assertion in the items test: a weapon whose stated reach disagrees with its mesh by more than 0.5 m is a lie the player can see and will learn to distrust. This is the single most checkable invariant in the whole physics section.
whatThePlayerActuallyFEELS.hitStopAndShakeAreMass: Both fields already exist on every combo step and both already follow the mass ordering (dagger 0.00 / sword finisher 0.05 / greataxe finisher 0.10 / maul finisher 0.12; shake 0.00 / 0.30 / 0.90 / 1.10). Keep the ordering monotonic in mass forever; assert it in the test so a tuning pass cannot invert it silently.
whatThePlayerActuallyFEELS.drawTimeIsMassToo: See stowDraw.drawTime — sheathing and drawing obey the same law as swinging, which is what stops stow/draw being a free cosmetic toggle.

projectilePhysics.currentState: game.js:1139 _spawnProjectile stores { mesh, pos, dir, speed, damage, life, color } with dir flattened by .setY(0).normalize(). game.js:1667 _updateProjectiles does pos.addScaledVector(dir, speed * dt), kills on life <= 0, on hypot(x,z) > world.radius + 2, and on obstacleField.blocked(x, z, 0.25, 0, pos.y). Player collision is a 1.1 m sphere test against the player at y 1.2.
projectilePhysics.requiredChange: Add optional `vy` (vertical velocity, m/s) and `g` (gravity, m/s^2) to the projectile record. Integration becomes: pos.x += dir.x * speed * dt; pos.z += dir.z * speed * dt; pos.y += vy * dt; vy -= g * dt. EVERY EXISTING CALLER PASSES g = 0 AND vy = 0, which reproduces today's flat integration EXACTLY — assert that byte-equality in the test rather than assuming it. Enemy caster bolts and boss spread shots must not change by a single float.

arrowNumbers.gravity: g = 9.0 m/s^2 — slightly under real gravity so aim stays forgiving on a phone without reading as floaty.
arrowNumbers.launchSpeed: 22 m/s at minimum draw, 46 m/s at full draw, linear in draw fraction.
arrowNumbers.launchElevation: The aim solver picks vy for a flat-ish arc to the soft-locked target; without a target, vy = speed * 0.12 (a gentle rise).
arrowNumbers.dropExample: At 46 m/s over 20 m the flight time is 0.435 s and the drop is 0.5 * 9.0 * 0.435^2 = 0.85 m. Visible, aimable, not annoying. At 22 m/s over the same distance the drop is 3.7 m, which is why a snapped-off shot misses and a drawn one does not — the player learns the draw from the arc, not from a number.
arrowNumbers.lifetime: 2.5 s (arrows outrun the 4 s bolt lifetime and would otherwise leave the disc cull first anyway).
arrowNumbers.damage: 0.55x weapon damage at minimum draw, 1.35x at full.

staffBoltNumbers.gravity: g = 9.0 — the SAME constant as arrows. That shared constant is the whole 'internally consistent magic' argument made visible: a bolt is slower, so it arcs more, so magic looks heavier than an arrow rather than looking like it broke a rule.
staffBoltNumbers.turnRate: 90 deg/s maximum, applied to the horizontal direction only. A stalker at 5.3 m/s can outrun a bolt at range; a brute at 2.3 m/s cannot.

performanceRequirements: POOL. 16 preallocated projectile records with 16 preallocated meshes, reused. The shipped code allocates an IcosahedronGeometry + a MeshBasicMaterial per shot and disposes them on removal; at bow cadence that is per-shot material creation, and weapons.js's own header measures a material-driven shader recompile at 8-60 ms on a mid-range Android.

NO PointLight per arrow. The shipped bolt parents `new THREE.PointLight(color, 2.2, 7)` to every projectile. Twelve arrows in flight is twelve dynamic lights, which is a cliff and not a cost. Arrows get a glow-layer material instead — the bloom pass already renders emissive-only geometry unlit, which is why edgeMat is MeshBasic.

Arrow geometry comes from mergedItemGeometry('Arrow') — the same bake-vertex-colour-and-merge path held weapons use, so an arrow is ONE draw call against the shared heldMaterial, not the 2-3 a naive getItemMesh clone would cost. Cache and flag userData.shared = true.
Cap live player projectiles at 12. Enemy projectiles keep their own budget.
projectilePhysics.lineOfSightUsage: Call obstacleField.lineBlocked(px, pz, tx, tz, { radius: 0.2, feetY: 1.4 }) ONCE at release, to validate the soft-lock target. Per-frame collision stays the existing obstacleField.blocked() at the arrow's own pos.y. The lineBlocked header is explicit that it is a throttled probe ('callers throttle (the AI probes on a 0.4 s cadence), never per-frame across the whole field') and firing three arrows a second, each probing every frame, is exactly the misuse it warns about.

rarityAndLegendary.ladder: UNCHANGED, and deliberately so. RARITIES in weapons.js: common (mul 1.00, 0 affixes, weight 100), uncommon (1.09, 1, 46), rare (1.20, 2, 18), epic (1.36, 3, 6), legendary (1.58, 4, 1.2). Do not add a sixth tier. Every UI colour, every price multiplier and every existing save already speaks this ladder.

whyLegendaryIsHarder.gate1_dropFloor: A legendary may not drop below rank band B (rankIndex >= 3). Implemented inside rollDrop / the loot path as a downgrade, not a re-roll: if the drawn rarity is legendary and rankIndex < 3, it becomes epic. A downgrade preserves determinism (the stream is consumed identically either way, exactly the trick rollWeapon already uses when a rarity is forced) where a re-roll would not. Effect: 'legendary' becomes a statement about where you have been, not about how lucky you were on your third E-gate.
whyLegendaryIsHarder.gate2_shopCeiling: The Exchange NEVER sells legendary. shopStock() currently rolls rarity with luck = band * 0.75, which at high bands makes legendaries genuinely likely on the shelf; clamp shop rarity to epic. Ash is a real currency with real sinks (respec, shadow promotion, and now the shelf) and letting it buy the top rung is how a shop turns into a slot machine you grind rather than a ladder you climb.
whyLegendaryIsHarder.gate3_ascension: A legendary is CRAFTED, not found. This is the direct answer to 'the legendary ones should be harder to develop'.

recipe: An EPIC instance of the family you want. It is consumed, and its seed becomes the legendary's seed — so the item you loved becomes the item you keep, and the save cost is still four fields.

9 EMBERDUST. A new consumable that only B-rank-and-above gates and Verge wild gates yield: 1 guaranteed per boss, plus a SEED-DERIVED chance per elite (derived from the gate's forked mulberry32 stream — never Date.now(), never Math.random(); this is the exact rule the randomised-enemy-count work is also bound by).

1 FAMILY SIGIL. One per weapon family, a guaranteed drop from a SPECIFIC boss: sword from the Hollow Warden, axe/greataxe from the Gravelord, dagger from the Frostcaller, greatsword from Infernus, bow from the Voidweaver, staff from the Rift Archon. Six families, six named bosses, no ambiguity about where to go.

whatMakesLegendaryMeaningfullyStronger.rawStep: Only +16% (1.36 -> 1.58). That is LESS than one tier step, which is roughly +53% in AP terms and comes with a genuinely different combo table. Stated plainly so nobody 'fixes' it upward: the raw multiplier is deliberately a small part of the prize.
whatMakesLegendaryMeaningfullyStronger.fourthAffix: Legendary is the only rarity with four affixes, drawn without replacement from a six/seven-entry pool — so a legendary is close to a full house of the good modifiers, which is a real and legible jump without being a bigger number.
whatMakesLegendaryMeaningfullyStronger.legendaryRule: The actual prize. One named clause per legendary base that changes a VERB. Hard law: A LEGENDARY RULE MAY NEVER MULTIPLY DAMAGE. Every one changes tempo, positioning or resource flow. That single constraint is what lets legendaries be exciting without being a balance event.
examples: RIFTEDGE ASCENDANT — your combo counter does not reset on a whiff, only when you take a hit.
DAWNBRAND ASCENDANT — the third chop's cancel window doubles, so the sword can loop its finisher into itself once.
SUNDERAXE ASCENDANT — the finisher's stagger applies to everything in the arc even on a miss (the wind alone staggers).
GRAVEMAUL ASCENDANT — the ground pound leaves a 3 s crater that halves enemy move speed inside it.
WHISPERFANGS ASCENDANT — a crit refunds 0.05 s of the current step's recovery, at most 3 times per combo.
VEINSPLITTERS ASCENDANT — bleeds applied by the offhand blade stack to 6 instead of 3.
VIGIL ASCENDANT — the thrust finisher passes THROUGH the first target and keeps its full damage on the second.
VOIDGLAIVE ASCENDANT — the sweep step also pulls every target 0.8 m toward the centre of the arc.
(greatsword) — a fully charged third step cannot be interrupted by anything below boss tier.
(bow) — a full-draw arrow that kills its target immediately refunds the draw.
(staff) — the channelled beam's mana cost stops rising after 0.8 s, so a long channel is cheaper per second than a short one.

stowDraw.ownerAsk: 'when they are in the plaza, the sword can be visible or placed in the inventory'
stowDraw.model: A transient STANCE on the character: 'drawn' | 'sheathed'. It lives on the player, not on the item, and it is NOT PERSISTED — a resumed save re-derives it from 'am I in the city and is anything near me'. Persisting it would create a third source of truth about what is in the hand, alongside save.equipment.weapon and root.userData.weapon.

policy.autoSheath: In the city or the Verge, with no hostile within 14 m and no attack input for 3.0 s, sheath.
policy.autoDraw: Any attack input, any hostile inside 14 m, or entering a gate. Draw is immediate in intent and takes drawTime to complete; an attack pressed during the draw is BUFFERED using the EXISTING state.buffered / consumeBuffer mechanism in weapons.js — do not invent a second input buffer.
policy.manualToggle: Long-press the attack button, and 'X' on desktop. This is the plaza show-off control the owner asked for, and it is the reason the auto policy needs a manual override at all.
policy.neverStowMidSwing: Refused while state.active or isCommitted(state, w). Both already exist.

drawTime.why: The mass law applied to one more verb. A greataxe player who lets the weapon sheath while wandering the Verge pays 0.35 s the moment something jumps him; a dagger player pays almost nothing. Without this, stow/draw is a free cosmetic toggle and mass stops being a consistent property of the world.

implementation.newSockets: characters.js gains sockets.back = makeSocket(getObjectByName(p + 'Chest'), { lift: 0, scale: 1 / MODEL_SCALE }) and sockets.hip = makeSocket(getObjectByName(p + 'Hips'), same). Both bones are confirmed present in the 62-bone list for both rigs. makeSocket is already generic — the only new thing is two calls.
implementation.proceduralFallback: entities.js rig gains back: rig.torso and hip: rig.body on the box-man path. The game must still boot with public/models/ deleted.
implementation.stowTable: weapons.js gains STOW[family] = { socket: 'back' | 'hip', x, y, z, rx, ry, rz }. A sword rides diagonally across the back (socket 'back', rz ~ 0.55, z ~ -0.16); a greatsword and greataxe ride the same way, larger; a bow rides flat and vertical on the back; TWIN DAGGERS RIDE AT THE HIPS (socket 'hip', one per side) — which is precisely why the entry carries a socket NAME and not just a transform.
implementation.api: export function setStance(root, stance) — resolves the current weapon group from root.userData.weapon, re-parents main (and offhand) between the hand socket and the stow socket, applies the corresponding transform, and calls root.userData.character?.setArmed?.(stance === 'drawn'). Returns the stance actually applied.
implementation.hardRule: RE-PARENT ONLY. No geometry is created, no material is created, nothing is disposed. weapons.js's asset-cache header measures a material dispose at 8-60 ms of shader recompile on a mid-range Android — 'a visible hitch on every weapon swap' — and a stow that rebuilt the mesh would pay that every time the player walked into the plaza.
implementation.freeWin: CharacterInstance.setArmed(false) already swaps the idle clip from Idle_Sword back to the neutral arms-down idle and invalidates the cached action so it takes effect immediately. Sheathing therefore produces the correct relaxed plaza walk with zero additional animation work.
implementation.npcs: Enemies, shadow soldiers, citizens and the city companion NEVER stow. They spawn drawn and stay drawn. One less state to test and zero risk to the crowd budget.

stowDraw.interactionWithEquipment: Stance is orthogonal to the equipment model. equipSlot('weapon', item) changes WHAT is held; setStance changes WHERE it is. Equipping while sheathed keeps the new weapon sheathed (and the panel shows it on the back, which is the honest read). The equipment model never stores stance.

wave3A_buildingNow.scope: Grip + stow/draw + inventory panel v1 with weapon slots. Everything needed for "the characters properly hold the swords", "in the plaza the sword can be visible or placed in the inventory", and "an inventory button that displays everything about the character". The armour slots exist in the panel but are rendered locked. STEP 1 IS NOT IN THIS WAVE — it was listed here, it was not built, and it has moved to 3-B where step 7 depends on it.
wave3A_buildingNow.shippableAlone: Yes, and it shipped. What it is NOT: "every weapon family finally feels different". That claim belonged to step 1 and step 1 did not land, so every family still swings on the sword's single 0.34 s timing with only damage / reach / arc / knockback multipliers separating them. What 3-A actually delivers is VISUAL and INFORMATIONAL: each family is held and stowed correctly, the sword goes on the back in town, and there is a character sheet you can equip from.

wave3B_next.scope: STEP 1 FIRST AND ALONE — wiring the swing state machine is carried over from 3-A and steps 7-9 are unreachable without it. Then armour, sets, and the new weapon families (greatsword, hand axe, bow with real projectile flight, staff), plus legendary gating and Ascension. STASH_LIMIT 12 -> 40 moves here too, alongside step 13's panel v2.
wave3B_next.shippableAlone: Yes, but with two units inside it: step 1 ships on its own commit before anything else touches combat, and steps 10-13 are a unit — armour tables without the damage integration and the panel are invisible.

risks: STEP 1 IS A FEEL REGRESSION RISK ON THE ONE THING THE OWNER JUST APPROVED. Wiring the swing state machine changes every attack in the game. Mitigation is structural: SWORD_COMBO is documented as byte-identical to the hardcoded swing, the step ships alone in its own commit, and the assert is numeric rather than a judgement call. If the assert cannot be made to pass, the table is wrong and the table gets fixed — the wiring does not get abandoned.

PHONE GPU BUDGET. Dungeons are capped at 24 draw calls and 130k tris, and this document adds a stowed weapon, arrows, and armour looks. Mitigations, each already chosen: stowed and drawn are the SAME merged mesh re-parented (zero extra draw calls, and a hidden second mesh is explicitly rejected because it still costs a matrix update and a frustum test); arrows share one merged geometry through the existing bake-and-merge path and are capped at 12 with no per-arrow PointLight; armour part-swap is player-only.

GPU LEAKS HAVE SHIPPED THREE TIMES IN THIS PROJECT. Every new cache entry must set userData.shared = true or entity teardown will free it out from under other holders; every new pool must register for disposal; the stance flip must create and dispose nothing, which is why the test asserts weaponCacheStats() equality across 100 flips rather than merely checking the parent.

SAVE COMPATIBILITY. Eight slots, a new stash field, and a materials bag all land in a save that must still load in the shipped build. Mitigations: no SCHEMA_VERSION bump (the shop/worldTime precedent), ensureEquipment idempotent and called first by every entry point, and save.weapon kept as a dual-written mirror so a rollback still finds the player's weapon.

412 PX LANDSCAPE OVERFLOW. The Exchange already had to be rebuilt as a scroll box for this exact viewport. The inventory has strictly more content. Mitigation: the two-column layout is designed against the 290 px of usable height, the row density is copied from shopui's tightened values, and the visual test gates it at 915x412 in both v1 and v2.

SET BONUSES TRIVIALISING THE GAME. This is the classic failure mode of the feature the owner asked for. Mitigations are three and all numeric: the partial-vs-rule asymmetry (small flat numbers vs one unstackable rule), the hard 0.72 total DR clamp and +0.6 armour speed clamp, and the L20/L50/L80 balance envelope assert that FAILS THE BUILD rather than merely warning.

THE PROJECTILE LOOP IS SHARED. Step 8 touches the same _updateProjectiles that enemy casters, boss spread shots and the Nova projectile-wipe all depend on. Mitigation: g = 0 and vy = 0 must reproduce the existing integration float-for-float, asserted over 240 steps, and the pool is introduced behind the same call shape.

MISSING ASSETS ARE A DESIGN CONSTRAINT, NOT A TODO. There is no staff, no spear, no shield, no helmet and no boots in items.glb, and no boot or leg ICON either. Any of these can quietly become 'we'll add the model later', which in an offline game with a curated pack means never. Mitigation: the staff is procedural by design and tested with the pack absent; the leg and foot icon mappings are flagged as an open question for the owner BEFORE 3-B starts rather than after.

SCOPE. Fourteen agent-sized steps is two waves, not one. Attempting 3-A and 3-B together is how a wave lands half-finished. The split above is chosen so 3-A is independently playable and independently shippable.

BOW AIMING VS A MELEE CAMERA. The orbit camera was tuned for melee and shipped four days ago. A ranged weapon wants a different aim affordance. Mitigation: no new camera mode this wave — soft-lock inside a 25 degree cone using the existing camera yaw. If that reads badly, it becomes its own wave rather than a late addition to this one.
openQuestions: BOW AIMING ON A PHONE. Recommended: soft-lock to the nearest enemy inside a 25 degree cone off the camera forward, no new input and no new camera mode. The alternative is a free-aim reticle, which needs a second thumb and a camera mode and is a wave of its own. Which does the owner want to feel?

ARMOUR SILHOUETTE. Does armour need to CHANGE HOW THE HUNTER LOOKS (character part-swap, 5 set looks x 2 rigs = 10 merged geometries, player-only) or is icon + stats enough for 3-B? Part-swap is the honest answer to 'collect a set' and is the only 3D expression available, but it is a real geometry cost and a real art-direction judgement.

LEG AND FOOT ICONS. There is no boot icon and no leg icon in the 108-key atlas. Options: reuse the set's chest icon desaturated, use bag/pouch as stand-ins, or draw two new icons into the atlas (tools/pack-icons.mjs already builds it, so this is cheap). This is the weakest mapping in the document and the owner should choose before step 10.

TRINKET SLOT: KEEP OR CUT? It is the best-supported slot in the whole pack (7 rings + 3 necklaces, all with icons) and it is the one slot no set can claim. But it is also an eighth slot on a 412 px screen. Recommended: keep.

DOES THE EXCHANGE SELL ARMOUR? Adding armour to the existing shelf roughly triples it (8 weapon rows -> 8 + 25). A second vendor — an Armoury door in the city, which the enterable-building system already supports — is cleaner but is new city content. Recommended: a second vendor, in a later wave; armour drops only until then.

WHERE DOES ASCENSION HAPPEN? The Exchange counter (zero new content, but a shop that also crafts is muddled) or a new Forge NPC / door (evocative, matches 'harder to develop', but is new city content and new dialogue)? Recommended: Forge, if there is room in 3-B.

SPEARS AND GLAIVES HAVE NO MODEL AND NO ICON. Ship them procedurally forever, or budget a small CC0 polearm pack? CONTENT_PACKS.json has no polearm entry at all, so this would be a new research pass. Recommended: procedural forever — buildPolearm already reads correctly and the pack budget is better spent elsewhere.

SHOULD STANCE BE REMEMBERED? Recommended NO — stance is transient and re-derived, because persisting it creates a third source of truth about what is in the hand. But the owner's phrasing ('the sword CAN be visible or placed in the inventory') might mean he wants the plaza to remember his preference. Worth one question.

TWIN DAGGERS AND THE OFFHAND. Daggers consume both hands, so the offhand slot locks. Is that acceptable, or should a single-dagger family exist so that dagger + focus / dagger + quiver becomes a build? Recommended: lock it in 3-B; revisit only if the offhand slot feels empty in play.

EMBERDUST AS A VISIBLE CURRENCY. It needs a HUD or panel home. The inventory STATS tab is the obvious place, but the owner may want it beside ash in the wallet strip. Cheap either way; ask before building both.
